reason: The 1890 founding cannot be told as a documented episode from pages that load. Every loading source reduces it to one hedged line: the Mumbai Dabbawala association's own site says a Parsi banker's lunch was carried by 'the first ever Dabbawala' and that Mahadeo Havaji Bachche later organised 100 men; the BBC says the idea is 'generally tracked back' to a Parsi banker and credits Bachche with organising about 100 workers in 1890, citing Shobha Bondre's book; Swarajya says 'it is said' Bachche himself first carried a Parsi businessman's meal; the Kerala textbook chapter (via ETV Bharat) says he carried the first box for a Parsi lady from Dadar to Fort. The sources disagree on the central event (who made the first delivery, and for whom), and none records what Bachche knew, decided or did next, so a 280-word story would need padding or invention. Bondre's book is not available online, and Atlas Obscura and the Harvard Business School case page are blocked for the verifier. A later, better-documented episode (the 2011 strike or the 2020 lockdown) would be about association leaders, not the founder or the founding, so it was not substituted.
